name: Modular / prefab housing
summary: Factory-built volumetric modules or panelized building systems, built to state/IRC/IBC codes (not HUD-code; see manufactured-home-community), then shipped and craned onto site-built foundations. The factory package is ~55–65% of hard cost. Transport, crane/set, foundations, mate-line finishing and site utilities are the rest. Published claims are of up to 20% hard-cost savings and 40–50% schedule savings (Terner Center 2017), but in practice cost is often near parity with site-built. No national cost series exists, so the default is derived as a ratio to site-built residential. Confidence is low-medium.

typicalSize.method: Units per project: from a few infill homes/ADUs to 3–4 story modular apartment buildings (100+ units, per the Terner Bay Area example of ~100 units in e1). Judgment.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Blend of modular apartments (~900 SF sample unit in e1) and modular single-family/townhomes (~1,500–2,000 SF; the Census site-built for-sale median of 2,216 SF caps the high). Module shipping widths (≤16 ft) favor compact plans. Judgment.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Detached modular at single-family densities (4–6/acre) up to 3–4 story modular walk-ups (30–40/acre). Mid reflects the townhome/small-multifamily mix. Judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Follows the comparable site-built product types. Judgment.

perSF.method: Ratio to site-built. The site-built residential baseline is ~$145–160/SF national (single-family mid $145, townhomes $150, duplex $160, per this category's files; 2025$). The modular/site-built ratio is 0.80–1.05. The low end is Terner's 'up to 20 percent' hard-cost saving (e1). The high end comes from LA 2026 builder pricing (e2): factory-only modular at ~$430/SF versus $640–710/SF stick-built. That is ~63% of site-built for the factory package, and adding foundation, set, utilities and site work (typically 30–45% of the module price) gives ~0.85–0.95× site-built. Mid ≈ 1.0× a $160 blended baseline, because published savings are mostly 'up to' claims and the industry 'has struggled to scale' (Terner 2026). Low $120 ≈ 0.8 × $150. High $230 for premium, design-forward prefab and high-cost-region delivery. Labeled 2026$ because the most recent evidence (e2) is 2026; the site-built baselines are 2025$.

scope.notes: Factory module/panel package incl. transport, plus crane and set, site-built foundations, mate-line and on-site finishing, utility connections and typical on-site work, incl. GC general conditions and OH&P. Excludes land, off-sites, impact/tap fees, A&E/engineering, factory deposit financing and FF&E.

qualityTiers.method: Economy = low/mid (120/160). Premium ≈ high/mid (230/160 = 1.44) tempered to 1.3. Luxury is judgment, for architect-designed prefab.

systemSplit.method: Div 13 (Special Construction: modular/pre-engineered structures) holds the factory package incl. transport at ~60%. That reflects the e2 factory-only price at ~63% of comparable site-built cost; Terner (e1) notes materials are ~60% of module cost. Div 01 holds GC general conditions plus crane/set. 03 = foundations/crawlspace; 07/09 = mate-line roofing and finishing; 22/23/26 = site MEP tie-ins between modules; 31–33 = site work and utilities. The site-side allocations are judgment.

lineItems.name: Module transport (factory to site)

cost.method: Per module (≈2 modules per unit). Oversize-load trucking within ~250–500 miles of the factory. Judgment; no public source found. Verify with the manufacturer's quote.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of Div 13. Rises sharply beyond ~500 miles.

cost.method: Judgment: crane day-rates plus set crew, spread over modules set per day. Mobilization dominates on small projects. Verify locally.

pctOfHard.method: Starts from the site-built residential soft-cost norm (~20%, see single-family). Less construction interest from a 40–50% shorter schedule: Terner cites ~2% of total construction cost saved on a $40M Bay Area project (e1). Offset by earlier design freeze, factory engineering and third-party inspection. Mid 18%. Judgment. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 5 points to follow the single-family norm with fees and financing removed. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Most states require third-party plan review and factory inspection under the state modular program. Factory deposits (~50% at order) shift financing earlier.

design.method: Design must freeze before factory production; late changes are costly. Judgment.

hard.method: Factory price is largely fixed, but site/set/mate-line risk and manufacturer-performance risk remain. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low: compact modular unit ~$100k hard × 1.14. High: large premium prefab home ~$415k × 1.3.

source.title: Building Affordability by Building Affordably: Exploring the Benefits, Barriers, and Breakthroughs Needed to Scale Off-Site Multifamily Construction
source.publisher: Terner Center for Housing Innovation, UC Berkeley

evidence.quote: off-site construction, as it is currently practiced, can save up to 20 percent on the cost of construction for a three or four story wood frame multifamily apartment building
evidence.scopeNotes: 'Up to' claim from developer evidence (2017). The same report: 'can reduce project construction time by between 40 and 50 percent'; a Bay Area 900 SF apartment 'costs an average of $350/square foot' site-built; manufacturers 'generally expect an upfront payment of 50 percent of the module cost'.

evidence.quote: The ~$430/sq ft is factory cost only. Foundation, utility connections, craning, site improvements, and decks are separate.
evidence.scopeNotes: Modular/steel-chassis custom home in a high-cost market, compared with stick-built at $640–710/SF hard in the same guide. Used for the factory/site-built ratio, not as an absolute.

source.title: A Deep Dive Into ADU Construction Costs: What the Per-Square-Foot Numbers Don't Tell You

evidence.scopeNotes: Small prefab ADUs (~400–900 SF); total project including installation. Corroborates the low end of the per-unit range.

openQuestions: McKinsey's 'Modular construction: From projects to products' (2019) and the Terner 2026 'Pathways to Scale Innovative Construction' report should be read for newer cost ratios; both fetches failed this session (timeout / unreadable PDF).
Public modular project budgets (e.g., modular supportive housing in Los Angeles or New York, HUD/state-funded modular pilots) would give direct per-unit hard costs.
Transport and crane/set line items are unsourced judgments.
